chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who claimed against her husband that he had divorced her with a single divorce, a valid divorce of the waiting period, meaning during purity from non-coitus, and witnesses testified for her regarding that. Then the husband denied it afterwards. So he (peace be upon him) said: If his denial of the divorce was before the completion of the waiting period, then his denial of the divorce is a revocation (raj'ah) for her. And if he denied the divorce after the completion of the waiting period, then it is upon the Imam (peace be upon him) to separate them after the testimony of the witnesses, after making him swear an oath that his denial of the divorce was after the completion of the waiting period, and he would be one of the proposers (from those who propose marriage).

key_terms.خَاطِبٌ مِنَ الْخُطَّابِ: One of the proposers (referring to the status of the divorced party in terms of remarriage proposals)
key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Revocation (the husband's right to take back his wife during the waiting period without a new contract)
key_terms.طَلَاقَ الْعِدَّةِ: Divorce of the waiting period (a single, valid divorce where the couple remains in a state of potential reconciliation)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a husband denies a divorce after the waiting period has ended?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential distinction between revocation (raj'ah) and judicial separation (talaq) based on the timing of the husband's denial relative to the waiting period (iddah). It highlights the Imam’s role in verifying the claim through witness testimony and the husband's oath, reflecting the Shia emphasis on procedural justice in marital disputes. The ruling underscores the legal finality of the iddah period as the threshold for determining whether the marriage bond remains intact or is dissolved by authority.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al Hannat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who claimed upon her husband, that he had divorced her with a divorce of the waiting period, being a correct divorce, meaning upon purity from without copulating, and witnesses testified for her upon that. Then the husband denied after that. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his denial of the divorce was before the fulfillment of the waiting period, so his denial of the divorce, there is reversion to her, and if his denial of the divorce was after the fulfillment of the waiting period, so it is upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he effects separated between them, both after the testimony of the witnesses, after having him swear on oath that his denial of the divorce was after the waiting period, and he would be a proposer from the proposers’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad al-Hannat who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who claims that her husband has divorced her once in the manner of divorce which requires a waiting period. That it has taken place in the presence of witnesses in a Hayd (menses)-free period and without going to bed, but the husband denies it. He (the Imam) said, Tf his denying is before the expiration of waiting period it is (his Ruju‘) going back to her but if it is after the expiration of waiting period, then it is the task of the Imam to separate them from each other after establishing testimony and after oath. His denying after the expiration of waiting period places him in the position of one of those who may propose marriage with her.’”
